pr_title: sql: add OID's to user defined types and populate pg_type
pr_body:
Fixes #48360.

This PR adds OID's to user defined types, and populates pg_type now
that user defined types have OID's.

I chose to represent type OID's using an offset from the type's
descriptor ID rather than to use a separate counter (this deviates from
the RFC a little). My rationale was as follows:
* There doesn't seem to be a benefit of introducing another kv counter
  for this information that already is within the descriptor ID.
* Since we can convert between ID and OID easily, this opens
  opportunities to easily add virtual indexes on OID, and do point
  lookups on descriptors wherever have just an OID.

Release note (sql change): The catalog table `pg_type` is now populated
with rows for user defined types (like enums).

issue_context.title: sql: populate pg_type table with user defined types
issue_context.body: The pg_type table needs to be filled with user defined types as well as the statically known set of types.

review_comments: Can we not avoid getting all descriptors somehow? or will this go away later? Just theoretically, could we get rid of that?
If (once) we have an index on system.descriptor we can. I also plan on adding a virtual index to this table, so that will be nice too.
This seems ... fine? Doesn't Postgres do something similar?

I'm not sure. Last time I looked, I saw that Postgres just has an oid pool that it takes from -- it will query the the target pg_catalog table when creating a new oid to see if it is not present before returning a new oid.
Do we need to worry that will give us headaches once we have oid pools?

I don't think so -- I left a comment where we allocate the table ID. If are in the space were allocated ID + this offset overflows, then we will just grab a new id from the descriptor free list (once that exists). If a new descriptor ID exists, then the corresponding type ID is free real estate.
